### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Bryant-Li-Bhoj neurodevelopmental syndrome 2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.464)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9764725)

**Proposed mechanism:** ZEB1 (HGNC:12713) —DISRUPTS→ transcriptional regulation of neuronal development (GO:0007409); transcriptional regulation of neuronal development (GO:0007409) —LEADS_TO→ neurodevelopmental abnormality (HP:0001263); H3-3B (HGNC:4774) —DISRUPTS→ histone modification and chromatin remodeling (GO:0016569); histone modification and chromatin remodeling (GO:0016569) —LEADS_TO→ developmental delay (HP:0001263); transcriptional regulation of neuronal development (GO:0007409) —BINDS→ histone modification and chromatin remodeling (GO:0016569). Haploinsufficiency of ZEB1 disrupts transcriptional regulation of neuronal development, leading to neurodevelopmental abnormalities. Similarly, haploinsufficiency of H3-3B disrupts histone modification and chromatin remodeling, contributing to developmental delay. The pathways of transcriptional regulation and histone modification are interconnected and both are critical for proper neuronal development, hence the overlap in disease modules.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in ZEB1 or H3-3B with a population frequency greater than 1% in gnomAD would cast doubt on their causal role in these rare diseases. Furthermore, if functional studies demonstrate distinct and non-overlapping molecular pathways downstream of ZEB1 and H3-3B that do not intersect, this hypothesis would be falsified.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic overlap in transcriptional regulation and chromatin remodeling provides potential therapeutic targets for both MONDO:0013206 and Bryant-Li-Bhoj neurodevelopmental syndrome 2. Strategies aimed at modulating these core processes could offer a unified therapeutic approach.

#### 2. Bryant-Li-Bhoj neurodevelopmental syndrome 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.425)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9764725)

**Proposed mechanism:** ZEB1 (HGNC:12761) —LEADS_TO→ Neurodevelopmental abnormalities (HP:0001263); H3-3A (HGNC:4775) —DISRUPTS→ Chromatin remodeling (GO:0006338); Chromatin remodeling (GO:0006338) —DECREASES→ Neuronal differentiation (GO:0030182); Neuronal differentiation (GO:0030182) —LEADS_TO→ Neurodevelopmental abnormalities (HP:0001263); Neuronal differentiation (GO:0030182) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249). Haploinsufficiency of ZEB1 (n1) leads to general neurodevelopmental abnormalities (n2). Loss-of-function mutations in H3-3A (n3) disrupt chromatin remodeling (n5), which in turn decreases proper neuronal differentiation (n4), ultimately causing neurodevelopmental abnormalities (n2) and intellectual disability (n6).

**How to falsify it:** Absence of evidence linking ZEB1 or H3-3A mutations to disruptions in neuronal differentiation or chromatin remodeling pathways in relevant model systems. _(variant: Presence of high-frequency (>= 1%) benign variants in ZEB1 or H3-3A in gnomAD that do not segregate with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared downstream pathways of ZEB1 and H3-3A in neuronal development could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both MONDO:0013206 and Bryant-Li-Bhoj neurodevelopmental syndrome 1, potentially through interventions aimed at modulating chromatin remodeling or neuronal differentiation processes.

#### 3. posterior polymorphous corneal dystrophy 3  —  Tier 5 — Refuted / Biologically Incoherent  (fitness 0.200)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:11642)

**Proposed mechanism:** Loss-of-function variants in ZEB1 (HGNC:11642) —DISRUPTS→ ZEB1 (HGNC:11642); ZEB1 (HGNC:11642) —DECREASES→ Corneal development and endothelial cell function (REACT:R-HSA-2437473); Corneal development and endothelial cell function (REACT:R-HSA-2437473) —LEADS_TO→ Anterior segment dysgenesis (HP:0000715); ZEB1 (HGNC:11642) —DECREASES→ Ocular development and morphogenesis (REACT:R-HSA-72148); Ocular development and morphogenesis (REACT:R-HSA-72148) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormalities of the eye (HP:0000475). **How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in ZEB1 with a gain-of-function mechanism for either disease, or the absence of any ZEB1 variants in affected individuals. _(variant: ExAC:3:14:ZEB1)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of ZEB1 in ocular development could lead to the development of targeted therapies for both posterior polymorphous corneal dystrophy 3 and related anterior segment dysgenesis disorders, potentially by modulating ZEB1 expression or its downstream targets.

#### 4. neurodevelopmental-craniofacial syndrome with variable renal and cardiac abnormalities  —  Tier 5 — Refuted / Biologically Incoherent  (fitness 0.200)
